title: Length-adaptive continuous scheduler with prefetch + eviction profiles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Improve the continuous batching scheduler to handle highly skewed mixed prompt/response length traffic by combining predictive prefetching of KV entries and length-adaptive eviction profiles to reduce tail latency and GPU memory churn.

Background: Production traffic shows heavy skew: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens) with long responses (>=512 tokens) and 30% multi-turn dialogs with alternating long/short segments. Current continuous-batcher sometimes pins KV pages for long dialogues causing memory pressure, or evicts too aggressively resulting in expensive KV reconstruction and p95 latency spikes during high load.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end p95 generation latency reduced by >=15% on mixed-length synthetic traces compared to baseline (runtime-1.25 config).
- GPU memory variance during 30min high-concurrency runs reduced by >=20% (fewer OOM near-misses).
- KV cache hit-rate improvement for long-response scenarios +10 percentage points without increasing mean latency for short prompts.

Approach:
1) Add a length-adaptive residency score per request slot that increases reservation for ongoing long-response jobs (KV warm) and decreases for ephemeral short ones.
2) Implement a lightweight prefix prefetch predictor trained on recent per-customer prompt histograms to pre-warm likely KV ranges during batching windows. Predictor lives in the scheduler with bounded memory and decays weights after 10 minutes.
3) Introduce eviction profiles: conservative (favor residency), balanced, and aggressive (favor density). Allow per-route overrides and automatic profile selection based on observed token-residency ratio.
4) Extend telemetry: add per-slot KV eviction reason, prefetch hits/misses, residency-duration histogram, and per-GPU slab fragmentation metric.
5) Offline tuning harness: synthetic traces generator that mirrors production skew and a runner to sweep eviction thresholds and prefetch window sizes.

Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated pool small-cust-2 (10% of weight) for 72 hours, compare metrics in console dashboard. If p95 improves and no increase in OOMs, expand to 50% then full. Fallback: per-route policy toggles to revert to baseline profile instantly.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/length-adaptive-continuous-scheduler (internal); tuning harness: https://git.redwood.ai/batching/tuning-harness (PR forthcoming).
